messages.author: 17f8070912132195
messages.subject: SPDE default prior
parts:
Hi all,

I was asked to report the default SPDE priors generated by the inla.spde2.matern function. I concluded that the default priors are:

log(tau)~N(1,10)
log(kappa)~N(?,10)

The default prior for log(kappa) depends on the mesh. How can I compute it? 

Thanks,
Ruby

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] SPDE default prior
parts:
Inla.spde2.pcmatern has more obvious priors (see doc). 

I don't remember what the default is in the range for the non-pc version. But I do remember that it's complicated to state.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] SPDE default prior
parts:
The default prior median range is a fifth of the approximate diameter of the mesh. You'll need to use the conversion formula to state that in terms of log(kappa)

The prior median for tau is also more complicated I believe.

You can check the numerical value for you particular model by looking at
spde$f$hyper.default

When using inla.spde2.matern you should really use the recipe given in the "read this first" spde tutorial instead of the default priors.  Or rather stop using the function, and use inla.spde2.pcmatern instead, like Daniel said.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] SPDE default prior
parts: On 9 Aug 2017, at 05:49, Daniel Simpson <dp.si...@gmail.com> wrote:
I thought the prior scale for tau was one (because you're not magic). Or is that the implied prior on the marginal variance?

The latter. Se the ?inla.spde2.matern documentation. The default is that it uses the default value 1 for the "prior.nominal.variance". That resulting prior median for log(tau) therefore depends on the prior median for kappa.

Finn

But yes: the PC variant exists because we weren't happy with the first defaults and tried to make them better.

Finn
